title: Build DefinePanel component
description:
Create `dashboard/frontend/components/landing/DefinePanel.tsx`.

Props: typed from the `define` field of LandingViewData (imported from landing.ts query types).

Sub-components (all within this file or split into the same directory):
- `PanelLabel`: renders 'Define' heading + 'Specs and preparation' subtext. Pattern reused by other panels so export it from a shared `PanelLabel.tsx`.
- `VisionWarning`: conditional dashed-border warning when `visionStatus === 'missing'`. Amber text using `--status-warning`.
- `DraftSpecItem`: icon + spec name + spec types badges + right arrow. Maps over `draftSpecs` array.
- `DefectList`: severity badges (P0 red, P1 amber, P2 secondary, P3 tertiary) + defect names.

Create `dashboard/frontend/components/landing/PanelLabel.tsx` as shared component.

Layout: vertical stack, 260px width (controlled by parent grid). Internal padding 20px. Use `.surface` class for card. 16px gap between sections.
acceptance_criteria:
- DefinePanel renders vision status warning when visionStatus is 'missing'
  verify_by: test
- DefinePanel hides vision warning when visionStatus is 'defined'
  verify_by: test
- Draft specs render with name, spec type badges, and arrow indicator
  verify_by: test
- Defects render with color-coded severity badges
  verify_by: test
- PanelLabel exported as reusable component with name and subtitle props
  verify_by: lint
- Empty state renders without errors when draftSpecs and defects are empty arrays
  verify_by: test
- Uses .surface class on card container
  verify_by: manual

spec_references.requirement: S3: Define panel with vision status, draft specs, and defect count
Panel labels follow Name → Intent pattern

rationale: DefinePanel is the left sidebar spanning full height. It's self-contained with no interaction mutations, making it a clean parallel unit alongside other panel components. PanelLabel is extracted here because DefinePanel is the first panel built, but all four panels will use it.
assumptions: Severity badge colors: P0 uses --status-error, P1 uses --status-warning, P2 uses --text-secondary, P3 uses --text-tertiary
decisions: PanelLabel accepts `name` and `subtitle` props (not `label`) — 'name' reads more naturally for a panel heading and matches how downstream tasks describe it ('Judge', 'Execute', 'Learn').

VisionWarning uses a dashed amber border rendered via inline style rather than a CSS class — the design token --color-amber is only available as a CSS variable, not a Tailwind class, and the dashed border is unique to this component.
DraftSpecItem uses the '→' text character for the right arrow rather than a lucide icon — keeps the dependency minimal and the spec only says 'right arrow indicator'.
SEVERITY_COLORS map covers P0–P3. The task assumptions note P0=error, P1=warning, P2=secondary, P3=tertiary. Implemented exactly as assumed.
Empty state message ('Nothing to review.') shown only when all three conditions are absent (no warning, no specs, no defects) to avoid showing it alongside content.
concerns: No testing framework (vitest + @testing-library/react) is installed in the frontend project — tests are syntactically correct but can't run until a vitest config and dependencies are added. Task 19 owns LandingPage.test.tsx and may establish the framework setup.
Test files are flagged as 'undeclared' by the gate scope check (warnings, not failures) since the task plan didn't list test files. This is cosmetic.
